battle.name: 藤原廣嗣之亂
battle.theater: 大和國越智驛至紀伊布祢
battle.brief: 天平十二年七月，藤原廣嗣與其父魚名、藤原萬紀及佐為王舉兵於備中國，東向經美作、但馬、播磨入大和；八月在越智驛與朝廷軍對峙，退入紀伊後於布祢崩潰，佐為王、萬紀戰死，廣嗣被擒下獄。卡面亞述短柄鐵鏃長矛早於本役一千六百年；奈良朝的短柄直槍與弓箭同樣以投射與密度取勝。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 天平十二年（740）七月起兵的一方，以藤原廣嗣為首。前右大臣、正一位藤原廣嗣與其父藤原魚名、藤原萬紀以及佐為王——一位經由聖武天皇正室光明一系與皇室相連的皇族——結成一體，後盾是備中國那珂郡的國司、郡司與鄉豪勢力。叛軍並非純粹的私兵集團：其核心是依律令調發的備中、備前兩國之兵，另有願意出兵的鄉豪部曲；動機最強烈的是那些在開墾事業中田產被沒收或重新丈量的豪族，事後證明，開墾才是真正的引爆點。廣嗣打出的口號，是奉佐為王為天皇、廢除自己受過的那份破格正一位；問題在於佐為王的血統雖足以充當人選，卻不足以讓全國國司承認。朝廷方面是孝謙天皇（聖武天皇之子）的中樞，但真正主導的是藤原道長。討逆軍由朝廷以中臣金連為大將軍，集合中臣、大伴兩姓的武門將領與藤原北家一系，統率畿內的大和、攝津、河內、山城、泉五國之兵，並徵發播磨、伊勢等近國的援軍；兵員、兵糧與馬匹皆由律令的調發體系供應。雙方分野極清楚：叛軍靠的是一縣之地的鄉豪與地方武力，朝廷靠的是全國性的國兵體制，加上首都的糧秣與馬匹。天平朝的律令國家尚未崩壞，這正是廣嗣輸掉這場叛亂的根本原因。
countriesEn: The side that rose in July of the Tempyō 12th year (740) was led by Fujiwara no Hirotsugu, the former right minister and the newly elevated shōichi. He was joined by his father Fujiwara no Uona, by Fujiwara no Maki, and by Prince Sadai, an imperial kinsman connected to the throne through Empress Kōmyō. Behind them stood the provincial officials, district officers and country magnates of Naka District in the province of Bitchū. The insurgents were not a purely private army: their core consisted of the levies of the two provinces of Bitchū and Bizen, called out under the ritsuryō apparatus, supplemented by the mounted retainers of local magnates. The most violent motive belonged to those whose fields had been confiscated or re-measured during the reclamation project; as it turned out, the reclamation scheme, not the throne, was the true fuse. Hirotsugu's stated program was to enthrone Sadai as emperor and to abolish the unprecedented grant of shōichi, the highest official rank, that he himself had received. The difficulty was that Sadai's blood, while enough to make him a candidate, was not enough to make the provincial authorities of the whole country accept him. On the court side stood the central government of Emperor Kōken, the grandson of Emperor Shōmu, but the man who in fact directed it was Fujiwara no Michinaga. The punitive expedition was organized by the court with Nakatsukasa Kaneshige as great general, drawing on the warrior clans Nakatsukasa and Ōtomo and on the northern Fujiwara line, and drawing in the levies of the five home provinces of Yamato, Settsu, Kawachi, Yamashiro and Izumi, together with reinforcements from Harima and Ise. Men, grain and horses all came through the ritsuryō dispatch system of the capital. The contrast was plain. The rebels could muster one county's local magnates and their private followers; the court commanded a national army system, plus the capital's granaries and stables. The ritsuryō state of the Tempyō era had not yet decayed, and that, more than anything else, is why Hirotsugu lost.
people: 藤原廣嗣是這場叛亂的靈魂。依《日本書紀》《續日本紀》通行的年表，他約生於天平初年，母為刑部比売（一般認為即天武天皇之女刑部皇女），父為藤原魚名，出身藤原北家，又兼具皇族血統。這樣的身世，使他能以二十餘歲接掌內大臣與右大臣兩職，並在740年獲授正一位——這是奈良朝絕無僅有的破格，也是他在朝中自居不可替代之身的根據。與他並肩作戰的是父親藤原魚名（從三位）、藤原萬紀，以及萬紀之子佐為王；佐為王是皇族近親，廣嗣起兵正是要把他推上皇位，自己則以攝政自居。朝廷一方的關鍵人物是藤原道長。他當時任中大臣，是「車爭」這場朝堂儀式的另一位主角：奈良朝天皇出行時，左右大臣爭著侍車左右，勝者居左。廣嗣以右大臣加正一位壓過道長，等於宣示了車爭的結果，這樁羞辱道長一方記了很久。討逆的實際統帥是中臣金連，他出身天武一系的中臣氏，是奈良朝典型的騎馬武門，與大伴氏同為皇室的武力支柱。包圍與追捕完成後，廣嗣與魚名被生擒，佐為王與萬紀在布祢陣亡。
peopleEn: Fujiwara no Hirotsugu was the soul of the rebellion. According to the standard chronology of the Nihon Shoki and Shoku Nihongi, he was born around the beginning of the Tempyō era; his mother was Gyōbu no Hi, generally identified with Gyōbu no Ōkimi, a daughter of Emperor Tenmu, and his father was Fujiwara no Uona. He thus belonged to the northern Fujiwara while also carrying imperial blood, a combination that let him take the posts of udaijin and udaijin of the right within a matter of years, and that in 740 brought him the grant of shōichi, chief first rank, the single most extraordinary promotion of the Nara period and the basis of his conviction that no one could replace him. Fighting beside him were his father Fujiwara no Uona, of the third rank and lower fourth grade, Fujiwara no Maki, and Maki's son Prince Sadai, an imperial kinsman whom Hirotsugu intended to place on the throne so that he himself might rule as regent. The decisive figure on the court's side was Fujiwara no Michinaga, then chūn daijin, the other principal of the kuruma arai, the carriage contest in which the two senior ministers fought over the place beside the emperor in his carriage, the victor taking the left. Outranking Michinaga as udaijin of the right and shōichi was, in effect, a public declaration of the outcome of that contest, and the humiliation was long remembered by Michinaga's side. The commander of the punitive force was Nakatsukasa Kaneshige, who came from the Nakatsukasa clan of the Tenmu line, the typical mounted warrior family of the Nara court and, together with the Ōtomo, one of the armed pillars of the imperial house. Once the pursuit and the cordon were complete, Hirotsugu and Uona were taken alive, while Sadai and Maki fell at Nuneyo.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長矛，是兩河流域冷兵器時代的短柄鐵刃長矛：短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃，與弓、鐵器並列為亞述人倚仗的裝備。亞述軍的骨架是三段式：密集的矛兵列在最前，以柳條編成的巨盾遮蔽身體，其後是射程極短的弓兵，兩翼與後方是騎兵。矛的價值不在單兵的廢殺力，而在把敵人的推進磨成對著盾牆的消耗；矛兵不追求刺穿，只追求在盾與盾的縫隙裡伸出去、把人頂回去。因此亞述矛必須成排使用，一個人拿著它獨自走出盾陣，幾乎等於送死。反觀天平十二年（740）的奈良朝，軍隊的主要投射手段是弓矢而非長矛。律令武官的隨身裝備是刀、弓、矢與短柄直槍——唐風長槍此時尚未普及，著律令甲冑、持手圓楯，騎馬者以武官為主，步兵的殺傷幾乎全靠弓矢的覆蓋射擊與短兵相接前最後一輪投射。徵兵按國、按郡、按里攤派，兵糧以粟為主、以牛車輸送，旗、檣、鉦鼓負責傳令與齊步。兩套體系並不矛盾：亞述式的短柄長矛提供的是「近戰靠密度」的原型，奈良朝則把密度交給弓陣與隊形，兩者同樣證明一件事——密集的正面與正確的信號，遠比單兵武藝決定勝負。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card is a short-shafted, long-bladed spear of the cold-weapon era of Mesopotamia: a short shaft, a long blade, an iron head, ranked alongside the bow and iron work among the equipment the Assyrians relied on. The skeleton of an Assyrian army ran in three lines: a dense front rank of spearmen screened by huge wicker shields, a body of short-range archers behind them, and cavalry on the flanks and in the rear. The value of the spear lay not in the killing power of the individual weapon but in grinding an enemy advance down against a wall of shields. The spearmen did not aim at piercing; they aimed at reaching through the gaps between shields and pushing the enemy back. A spear therefore had to be used in ranks, and a man who carried it out of the shield line on his own was very nearly a corpse. Look again at the Nara court of 740, and the main missile of its army was the bow and arrow, not the spear. The equipment of a ritsuryō officer was the sword, the bow, the arrow and the straight short spear, the long Tang-style spear not yet being in general use, together with ritsuryō armour and a small round shield; the mounted men were the officers, and the killing of the infantry was almost entirely the work of archery, both in the covering volleys and in a last shower of arrows before the lines closed. Levies were apportioned by province, by district and by village; the grain was millet, moved on ox carts; banners, standards and drums carried the orders and kept the step. The two systems are not contradictory. The Assyrian short spear supplies the archetype of close fighting won by density; the Nara court entrusted density to the arrow line and to formation. Both prove the same thing: a dense front and correct signalling decide a battle far more than the martial skill of any single man.
tactics: 叛軍的作戰方式，最能說明地方私兵的極限。廣嗣等在備中國那珂郡集兵，既無調發令，又無準備時間，只能靠郡司、鄉豪出錢出人；兵員雜而不齊，騎兵比例偏低，許多鄉兵甚至沒有制式鎧甲，只持短柄直槍與農具改製的器物。開拔時以令旗、檣相連，斥候先行，沿備前、美作、但馬、播磨的山道東行，強徵沿線郡倉的粟作為兵糧，用牛車輸送；行軍縱列極長，縱隊一旦被截斷就各自潰散。朝廷軍的戰法完全不同。金連以近國兵為主力，先以騎兵與快速部隊切斷叛軍的糧道與退路，再以大隊在越智驛正面壓制；同時利用廣嗣名位上的正統性，向叛軍中的皇族與國司派遣詔書，說明奉佐為王並無朝廷詔命，從而動搖那些只是被裹挲的鄉豪。廣嗣在越智驛接到朝廷的勅書後，指其文體不合詔敕、疑為偽造，反而以此宣布朝廷無意恩赦，下令進攻——這一判斷使叛軍放棄了最後一次不流血收束的機會。戰局轉折在追擊：叛軍退入紀伊國，朝廷軍連夜追入狹窄山道，在布祢一帶攻破其陣，佐為王、萬紀當陣自刃，廣嗣與魚名被生擒。事後朝廷分遣使者到伊賀、伊勢、越前等國搜捕同謀，斬首、流刑、沒收田戶，並把戰報與刑罰公告天下，以示律令國家不容私兵挑戰。
tacticsEn: The way the insurgents fought shows the limits of a provincial private army better than any number could. Hirotsugu and his confederates mustered in Naka District of Bitchū with neither a call-up warrant nor time to prepare, so the men had to be bought with money and pressed out of the district officers and country magnates. The ranks were mixed and uneven, the proportion of cavalry was low, and many of the country men had no regulation armour at all, carrying only straight short spears and tools beaten up from farm implements. On the march the columns were held together by order flags and standards, with scouts out in front, moving east along the mountain roads through Bizen, Mimasaka, Tajima and Harima; they seized the millet from the district granaries along the way and moved it on ox carts, and the marching columns were so long that once one of them was cut the whole thing came apart. The court's method was entirely different. Kaneshige took the levies of the nearby provinces as his main force, sent cavalry and fast troops ahead to cut the rebels' line of supply and their retreat, and then pressed them in a formed body at the post station of Ōchi. At the same time he used the legitimacy of Hirotsugu's own rank, dispatching imperial messages to the princes, provincial officials and district officers among the rebels to make it clear that no court order had ever enjoined the enthronement of Sadai, and so shaking the country magnates who had only been swept along. When Hirotsugu received the court's edict at Ōchi he declared that its form did not answer to an imperial rescript and suspected it of forgery, and on that basis announced that the court intended no pardon, ordering the attack. That judgement cost the rebels their last chance to end the affair without blood. The turning point came in the pursuit: the rebels withdrew into the province of Kii, the court army followed them into the narrow passes by night, broke their formation around Nuneyo, where Sadai and Maki killed themselves on the field, and Hirotsugu and Uona were taken alive. Afterwards the court sent envoys to Iga, Ise, Echizen and other provinces to hunt down the remaining conspirators, executing, exiling and confiscating them, and published both the reports of the campaign and the sentences, to show that a ritsuryō state would not tolerate the challenge of private military power.
data: 時間表很短：起兵在天平十二年七月，《續日本紀》記其時兵鋒已及紀伊、大和；朝廷軍抵達越智驛在八月，兵敗被擒亦在八月，全程不足一個月。行程方面，備中國那珂郡至大和國境約二百餘里，東行橫穿美作、但馬、播磨、攝津數國；退入紀伊後再戰於布祢，距大和不出數十里。兵員沒有確數：《續日本紀》只說叛軍徵發備中、備前諸國之兵，量級在數千至萬餘之間，具體點數史家多持保留；朝廷方面除畿內五國外另有播磨、伊勢等處應募，總數遠多於叛軍，所以這從來不是兵力相當之戰。官秩方面，廣嗣的正一位在他下獄後即告罷，奈良朝此後再無第二人獲授此位，這一空缺一直延續到明治年間重新用於天皇與皇族。開墾方面，740年正是廣嗣擔任開墾總監之年；事敗後朝廷廢止墾田、把田地歸還里戶，743年重新施行班田收授，奈良朝的田制由此回到原點。人物結局方面，佐為王與萬紀死於布祢，廣嗣在獄中不久而亡，魚名在獄中又坐了十七年，至757年才死。戰後朝廷依律處斬、流刑同謀，並沒收其田宅家產。
dataEn: The timetable was short. The revolt began in the seventh month of the Tempyō 12th year; the Shoku Nihongi records that by then its spearhead had already reached Kii and Yamato. The court army reached the post station of Ōchi in the eighth month, and the defeat and the captures likewise fell in that eighth month, so the whole affair lasted less than a month. As for distance, the march from Naka District in Bitchū to the borders of Yamato is on the order of a little over two hundred ri, running east through Mimasaka, Tajima, Harima and Settsu; the flight back into Kii and the second battle at Nuneyo lay no more than a few dozen ri from Yamato. There are no exact numbers of men. The Shoku Nihongi says only that the insurgents levied the troops of the provinces of Bitchū and Bizen and their like, a magnitude somewhere between several thousand and a little over ten thousand, and historians keep a reserve on the precise figures; on the court side the five home provinces were joined by contingents from Harima, Ise and elsewhere, so the court's numbers were far larger and this was never an even contest. As for rank, Hirotsugu's shōichi was withdrawn as soon as he was imprisoned, and no one else in the Nara period ever received it; that vacancy lasted until the Meiji era, when it was revived for the emperor and the imperial family. As for the reclamation, 740 was the very year in which Hirotsugu served as director of the project; after the disaster the court cancelled the reclaimed fields, returned the land to the households, and in 743 restored the allotment system, putting the Nara land system back where it had been. As for the men, Sadai and Maki died at Nuneyo, Hirotsugu died soon after entering the prison, and Uona spent seventeen more years in his cell, dying only in 757. After the campaign the court executed and exiled the conspirators under the law and confiscated their fields, houses and property.
cause: 起事並非出於一場軍事危機，而是權力分配與土地政策的雙重擠壓。政治上，藤原氏本身已分成兩房，廣嗣代表的魚名系與道長代表的另一派在奈良朝那套車爭儀式上正面對撞：天皇出行時左右大臣爭侍車之位，勝者居左，敗者受車輪之辱。廣嗣以右大臣、正一位壓過居中大臣的道長，等於宣示車爭的結果；對道長一派而言，廣嗣不只是同族，更是奪走朝廷中心位置的人。他的血統又格外扎眼——母系為天武天皇之女——這讓廣嗣自認可以光明正大地攝政，無須借助佐為王的血統。經濟上，740年朝廷推行開墾，把墾田集中為國有公田並重新分派佃種，觸動備中國等處國司、郡司與鄉豪的既有利益，手段峻急，全國怨謗集中到主持開墾的廣嗣一身。開墾成效不佳、朝議的責難隨之而來，廣嗣被解職，唯恐失位。他於是把開墾中結怨的地方豪族拉到自己一方，用廢正一位、奉佐為王為號召，把對朝廷的怨憊轉化成一場倉促的私人起兵；而天平末年接連的歉收與疫病，又讓鄉里的騷動更容易被煽動成集體行動。
causeEn: The rising was not born of any military emergency but of a double pressure, one of political distribution of power and one of land policy. Politically the Fujiwara had themselves split into two houses, and the line of Uona represented by Hirotsugu had collided head-on with Michinaga's line in the Nara court ritual of the carriage contest: when the emperor travelled, the two senior ministers fought for the place beside him, the victor taking the left and the loser humoured by the wheels. Hirotsugu, as udaijin of the right and shōichi, outranked Michinaga the chūn daijin, which amounted to a public pronouncement of the result of that contest; to Michinaga's side, Hirotsugu was not merely a kinsman but the man who had taken the centre of the court from them. His blood was unusually good as well, for his mother descended from a daughter of Emperor Tenmu, which allowed him to believe that he could rule as regent in his own right, with no need for Sadai's claim at all. Economically, in 740 the court pressed ahead with the reclamation project, concentrating the new fields into state land and redistributing the right to cultivate them. This struck at the existing interests of the provincial officials, district officers and magnates of Bitchū and other provinces, and the methods were severe, so that the resentment of the whole country came to rest on Hirotsugu, who was himself directing the work. When the scheme went badly and the criticism of the assembly followed, he was relieved of his post, and he feared for his position. He therefore drew the magnates who had been injured by the reclamation to his side, and used the demand to abolish the shōichi and to enthrone Sadai as a rallying cry that turned resentment against the court into a hastily raised private army; and the poor harvests and the epidemics that marked the closing years of the Tempyō period made it far easier to stir the villages into collective action.
impact: 這場叛亂的結果，是奈良朝權力結構的一次重新洗牌。魚名一系的覆滅，使以道長為首的藤原氏另一支得以獨占中樞，此後藤原氏內部南北兩家輪流掌權的格局由此定型，藤原外戚政治也從內部均衡走向一方獨大，直到平安朝初期才被武家勢力徹底取代。制度上留下三道痕跡。其一，開墾政策廢止，墾田歸還里戶，743年班田收授重新施行，奈良朝一度向公田制靠攏的嘗試被逆轉。其二，正一位在廣嗣之後成為空位，奈良朝再未有人獲授，直到明治年間才重新用於天皇與皇族，說明當時朝議確實把它視為不可再犯的破格。其三，討逆過程中中臣、大伴兩姓的武門成為朝廷兵力的骨幹，藤原氏近乎純文官的形象被打破，宮廷每年例行派遣中臣、大伴率兵入京宿衛的制度由此確立，文人朝廷、兵力仰賴外家的格局預示了平安朝藤原為平、源平為武的分野。在兵器史上，這場戰鬥也提供了一個有意思的對照：一方是靠弓矢投射加密集隊形取勝的奈良朝國兵，一方是廣嗣倚仗的鄉豪私兵。兩者都說明密集的正面、統一的信號與充沛的兵糧，遠比將領個人的武藝更決定戰局；而亞述短柄長矛所代表的近戰密度原型，恰好也提醒人們：長矛從來不是靠個人發揮取勝的兵器。
impactEn: The outcome of the rebellion was a reshuffling of the Nara political structure. The destruction of Uona's line let the other branch of the Fujiwara, the one headed by Michinaga, hold the centre of the court by itself, and the pattern by which the northern and southern houses of the Fujiwara would take turns at power dates from this moment. Fujiwara regency politics moved from an internal balance towards the monopoly of one side, and was not displaced by warrior families until the opening years of the Heian period. Three institutional scars remain. First, the reclamation project was abandoned, the reclaimed fields returned to the households, and the allotment system restored in 743, reversing the Nara court's brief experiment with a public-field system. Second, shōichi became a vacant rank after Hirotsugu; no one in the Nara period received it again, and it was not revived for the emperor and the imperial family until the Meiji era, which shows that the assembly of that time did regard the grant as a transgression never to be repeated. Third, the warrior clans Nakatsukasa and Ōtomo became the backbone of the court's forces during the punitive campaign, breaking the almost purely civil image of the Fujiwara and establishing the routine by which the Nakatsukasa and the Ōtomo escorted troops to the capital to hold the palace guard each year; a court of literati leaning on the military service of its own relatives pointed forward to the Heian division of Fujiwara for peace and Minamoto and Taira for war. For the history of arms the campaign also offers an instructive contrast: on one side a Nara national army that won by arrow volleys and dense formation, on the other the private retainers Hirotsugu could hire. Both make the same point, that a dense front, uniform signalling and ample supply decide a battle far more than the individual skill of commanders; and the short Assyrian spear, the archetype of density in close combat, is a reminder that the spear was never a weapon won by individual performance.
result: 天平十二年八月，朝廷軍在越智驛正面壓倒叛軍，追入紀伊國於布祢一帶攻破其陣。佐為王與藤原萬紀相繼自刃，藤原廣嗣與藤原魚名被生擒，解送京師囚於大牢。廣嗣的正一位隨即被罷，官位、封戶與田宅一併追奪；其餘同謀按律處以斬刑與流刑，田宅沒收入官。廣嗣在天平十五年（743）前後卒於獄中，魚名在獄中又度過十七年，至天平勝寶九年（757）才死。整場叛亂從七月起兵到八月平定，前後不足一個月，天皇的統治未受動搖，反而因平亂而更為鞏固。車爭的勝負也在此役分出：廣嗣的敗亡等於宣告道長在朝堂競爭中的最終勝利，他此後一路升遷，最終在攝政之位上奠定藤原家在平安初年的百年基業；而那面用來承載天皇、承載左右大臣之爭的車，則在奈良朝的尾聲裡安靜地停下，成為此後三百年間藤原家輪流坐上去的那一輛。
resultEn: In the eighth month of the Tempyō 12th year the court army beat the insurgents in a formed confrontation at Ōchi, followed them into the province of Kii and broke their line around Nuneyo. Prince Sadai and Fujiwara no Maki killed themselves in turn, while Hirotsugu and Uona were taken alive, carried to the capital and shut up in the great prison. Hirotsugu's shōichi was revoked at once, his offices, his fief and his fields and houses all stripped away; the remaining conspirators were dealt with under the law, by execution and exile, their property taken into the treasury. Hirotsugu died in prison around the Tempyō 15th year (743), and Uona spent another seventeen years in his cell, dying only in the Tempyō Shōhō 9th year (757). The whole revolt, from the rising in the seventh month to its suppression in the eighth, lasted less than a month; the emperor's rule was not shaken by it, and was made firmer by it. The carriage contest was decided as well: Hirotsugu's fall pronounced the final victory of Michinaga in the struggle at court, and Michinaga rose steadily afterwards, ultimately establishing at the regency the century-long foundation of the Fujiwara in the early Heian years; the carriage that carried the emperor, and the rivalry of the two ministers for the place at his side, came quietly to a halt in the closing days of the Nara period, ready to be taken in turn by the Fujiwara for the three hundred years that followed.
